A1.justification: Both PDFs contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices for the same reward-redistribution research, renamed from R3HF to RED. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched despite substantial revision.

before.justification: Sections 4 and Appendix C report original model-training experiments, reward scores, GPT-4 evaluations, learning curves, and generated examples.

after.justification: Sections 4 and Appendix C report original training results, ablations, human evaluations, reward-quality assessments, and generated examples.

M1.justification: The core temporal-difference redistribution remains unchanged. v2 adds a convex combination of redistributed token rewards and the original terminal reward, controlled by beta_c in Equation 7. This changes the training reward in configurations using beta_c below one, while retaining the existing reward model and central algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions use Nectar, TL;DR, SafeRLHF, and Alpaca for the same question-answering, summarization, and helpfulness/harmlessness tasks. New model configurations, human assessments, and reward-perturbation controls retain this dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds attention-based credits (ABC) and RLOO comparisons, including PPO-ABC and RLOO-ABC on Nectar and TL;DR. LLaMA3 comparisons also gain DPO and, on SafeRLHF, Lagrangian variants. The earlier uniform terminal-reward Simple baseline disappears. These substantially expand and revise the evaluated comparator sets.

E3.justification: Appendix B changes Nectar reward-model training from 5,000 to 102,366 examples and broadens preference-pair construction. TL;DR SFT/RL counts change from 14,900/14,900 to 116,722/92,846, with revised learning rates, lengths, and other hyperparameters. Qwen2.5 configurations replace GPT-J evaluations, and human-evaluation and coherence/diversity protocols are added. These are reported setting changes, without establishing which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds reward-mixture ablations, return-preserving reward-noise tests, a dynamic-initialization control, human assessment of token-credit quality, coherence/diversity analyses, and reward–KL relationships. Its initialization control redistributes the prompt offset and is distinct from v1's removed uniform terminal-reward baseline. Case studies are also expanded and revised.

E5.justification: v1 explicitly reports three random seeds and train/test error bars in Section 4.6 and Figure 4. v2 removes that disclosure, labels learning-curve bands as standard deviations, and adds ablation error bars without specifying their repeated-run basis. This changes uncertainty reporting but does not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: Many reported scores are replaced: for example, LLaMA Nectar PPO-R3HF's reward score/win rate of 3.9008/92.72% becomes PPO-RED's 3.475/97.83% in Table 1. Changed training settings prevent interpreting these as same-setting performance changes. v2 also adds ABC, RLOO, Qwen2.5, human-evaluation, and ablation results, while removing GPT-J results.

T1.justification: v2 adds a potential-based-shaping proof involving value-function shifts and unchanged advantages, explicit stochastic-approximation assumptions in Appendix A.2, and derivations for the mixed reward's return. The earlier DPO analysis is largely retained and relocated; the new proof and formal conditions constitute substantive theoretical additions.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that token-level credit from an existing reward model improves RLHF with little overhead, requires no additional fine-grained human labeling or reward-model retraining, and preserves the optimal policy. RED's name and stronger emphasis on computational simplicity reframe claims already present in v1.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations for ABC's weaknesses, RLOO's behavior, and reward–cost conflicts. It newly acknowledges missing token-reward ground truth and difficulty rewarding reasoning steps in coding/math, while removing the no-human-evaluation limitation after adding human studies. The stability discussion also shifts from reduced fluctuations to acknowledging greater variability.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds implementation pseudocode, model-specific parameter tables, explicit KL coefficients, RLOO sample counts, mixture weights, and human-questionnaire templates. Dataset construction and training instructions are revised. Hardware/timing information and GPT-4 prompts remain, while the explicit cost-model training loss is replaced by a reference to prior work.

R1.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A.2 substantially expand positioning around fine-grained rewards and RL alternatives. Chan et al.'s ABC becomes the closest comparator, alongside new discussion and citations covering KTO, SimPO, ORPO, REINFORCE variants, and GRPO/DeepSeek. Earlier Xia and Zhong comparisons are retained and relocated.

P1.justification: The paper is retitled and renamed, with extensive rewriting of the abstract, method explanation, experimental narrative, related work, and limitations. DPO/concurrent-work discussions and stability/showcase material move into the appendices, while the main text gains a dedicated ablation section and reorganized explanatory subheadings.

P2.justification: The main text switches to two columns, Figure 1 is redrawn, and new reward-computation, ablation, and pseudocode figures appear. SafeRLHF results move from a plot to expanded tables; learning curves become a multi-panel reward/KL analysis. Results tables are consolidated and expanded with model groupings, human assessments, and additional showcases.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses v1's explicit lack of human evaluation through Appendix C.2/C.5 and Table 13, and adds the closely related ABC comparator plus controlled reward-noise and initialization tests. These substantially strengthen assessment of the central credit-assignment and alignment claims. Removal of seed-count reporting and inconsistent win/tie/loss totals in some new tables temper confidence in individual comparisons, but the added direct validation provides a substantial overall benefit.
